principle: TTF learns from training species without seeing the named boundary. External biogeographic boundary geometry is frozen prospectively and used only after held-out transfer scoring.
admissibility: important biogeographic boundary defined independently of the focal trait
multiple replicate species or systems when used for a cross-species TTF claim
georeferenced observations or prospectively frozen geographic population units spanning the relevant domain
trait measurement not selected or tuned using TTF response
species inclusion frozen before TTF outcomes are inspected
external boundary geometry frozen before final scoring
primary TTF field is fit blind to the named boundary
pairwise genetic distance matrix cells are never shuffled

benchmarks.boundary_system: south-east Queensland freshwater river-basin biogeographic frontiers
benchmarks.trait_domain: mitochondrial sequence genetic distance among basin populations
benchmarks.replicate_units: 33 freshwater species (23 fishes, 10 crustaceans); 1814 source sequences across 8 basins

source.citation: Page & Hughes 2014, Biological Journal of the Linnean Society 111:554-569

benchmarks.observation_contract: aggregate source sequences within species x basin; each populated basin is one geographic observation for that species; graph construction is within species only
benchmarks.distance_contract: prospectively compute basin-population genetic dissimilarity from archived aligned mitochondrial sequences; exact metric is frozen before empirical TTF scoring, with raw p-distance as a transparent candidate and source-compatible genetic distance as robustness if reconstructable
benchmarks.geometry_contract: basin locations/centroids are frozen independently of genetic outcomes; Mary-Brisbane is not supplied to field fitting and is used only for later external concordance
benchmarks.eligibility_draft: species retained solely by basin support: enough non-empty basin populations to construct at least 3 unique geographic edges; no filtering by lineage depth, published divergence, PhiST, or TTF score
benchmarks.qualification_plan: first run shared/private semi-synthetic worlds on the exact retained species-by-basin geometry; only a type-I/power-qualified design may open empirical sequence-distance TTF outcomes
